done_when: forge sync writes every generated file in any worktree, whatever other worktrees hold, and never refuses for another worktree's spec

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The new skip covers ambiguous ownership, but `preserve_chats` still runs before generated files are written (`src/forge/sync.py:525`) and still refuses when another worktree's reader notes have uncommitted edits (`src/forge/codex.py:345-346`) or an earlier-release read holds the chat (`src/forge/codex.py:334-338`). In either ordinary upgrade case, `forge sync` exits before refreshing the requested worktree's host skills. The existing dirty-notes test at `tests/test_worker_and_reader_chats_survive_rounds.py:219-230` confirms this refusal.
findings.title: Not done: forge sync writes every generated file in any worktree, whatever other worktrees hold, and never refuses for another worktree's

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The named `test_1_sync_writes_generated_files_while_two_worktrees_hold_one_spec` deletes and checks only `.claude/skills/forge/SKILL.md` (`tests/test_sync_in_any_worktree.py:35-40`), including in its Codex-reader cases. It would pass if sync stopped writing the Codex guide or another generated file in this multi-worktree condition. The proof list also claims recovery when Codex has no starting commit, but that case returns after checking only the notice and absence of committed notes (`tests/test_spec_chat_upgrade_amendment.py:97-101`); it would pass if the next read started a new chat.
findings.title: Not done: the command-level sync proof

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss. On ambiguous ownership, sync now succeeds while leaving the earlier reader binding solely under the shared `.git/forge/threads` directory (`src/forge/codex.py:296-300` and `src/forge/codex.py:779-785`). The shipped guide says to keep `.git/forge` until the upgrade finishes (`src/forge/templates/skill.md:1010`); a normal upgrade can finish without reading that spec. Removing the local records afterward loses the binding because neither branch received it. The new test proves resumption only while those records remain, unlike the neighboring upgrade test, which deletes `.git/forge` before checking recovery (`tests/test_worker_and_reader_chats_survive_rounds.py:819-828`).
findings.title: Successful sync can leave the only reader binding in disposable local records

why: forge sync still refuses in a worktree when another worktree holds a copy of a spec, so builders copy the guide by hand into both host skill files
